chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to him: Blood is on the garment I am wearing while I am in salat (prayer). He said: “If you see it and you have another garment besides it on you, then cast it off and pray. If you do not have another garment on you, then continue in your salat (prayer), and there is no repetition upon you. Whatever does not exceed the measure of a dirham of that is nothing, whether you saw it or did not see it. But if you had seen it and it was more than the measure of a dirham, and you neglected washing it and prayed in it many prayers, then repeat what you prayed in it.”

key_terms.الثَّوْبِ: the garment or clothing being worn in prayer
key_terms.الدَّمُ: blood found on the garment during salat (prayer)
key_terms.غَسْلَهُ: washing the blood from the garment
key_terms.فَأَعِدْ: repeat the prayers performed in that state
key_terms.فَاطْرَحْهُ: remove or cast off the garment
key_terms.مِقْدَارِ الدِّرْهَمِ: the threshold amount used to determine legal consequence
key_terms.وَلَا إِعَادَةَ عَلَيْكَ: there is no obligation to repeat the prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying with blood on one's clothes if it is noticed during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about blood on clothing during salat (prayer). It explains when one should remove the garment, when one may continue the prayer, and when past prayers must be repeated depending on the amount of blood and prior awareness of it.
